# Foothold Now

> Foothold Now (grhs24.github.io) is a quiet website for building practice
> ladders—also called fear ladders, anxiety ladders, OCD ladders, or exposure
> hierarchies. You break something you avoid into small steps written in your
> own words, rate each step 0–100 (a SUDS rating—Subjective Units of Distress),
> practice on purpose, and log how it felt before, at the peak, and after.
> Ratings fall with repetition; a step that reaches zero settles. The method is
> rooted in exposure and response prevention (ERP) and graded exposure, with
> strong evidence for easing anxiety and the obsessions and compulsions of
> OCD—no diagnosis is needed to use it. Data stays in the browser
> (localStorage); nothing is uploaded. Foothold Now is free. It is a personal practice
> companion, not medical care.

## App

- [Foothold Now](https://grhs24.github.io/): the practice-ladder website itself.

## Guides

- [Exposure hierarchy (fear ladder): what it is and how to build one](https://grhs24.github.io/fear-ladder/): the tool under all its names—fear ladder, anxiety ladder, OCD ladder—with a worked example and honest tips.
- [ERP therapy, explained gently](https://grhs24.github.io/erp/): exposure and response prevention in plain language—the two halves of the name, the evidence, the history from Wolpe to Meyer, and what practice feels like.
- [Sample exposure ladders](https://grhs24.github.io/sample-ladders/): three ready-made ladders—just-right, perfectionism, and avoidance—adapted from ERP literature (Foa/Yadin/Lichner, Antony & Swinson, Coles et al., Abramowitz) with SUDS ratings, each addable to the app in one tap and meant to be reworded and re-rated by the user.
- [Using your notes to map an OCD loop](https://grhs24.github.io/ocd-notes/): unpack the OCD cycle in writing—obsessions and urges, the feared outcome, physical and mental compulsions, avoided situations, and a response-prevention rule per step, with a copyable six-field note template.
- [The SUDS scale (Subjective Units of Distress), explained](https://grhs24.github.io/suds/): the 0–100 distress rating created by Joseph Wolpe—example anchors, why subjectivity is the point, and how it powers exposure practice.
- [How to stop avoiding things](https://grhs24.github.io/stop-avoiding/): the avoidance loop (relief now, interest later) and the graded way out.

## Privacy

- [Privacy](https://grhs24.github.io/privacy/): ladders stay in the browser and nothing is uploaded. No accounts, no data selling, no profiles, no analytics.

## About

- [Why I created Foothold Now](https://grhs24.github.io/about/): the founder’s story—Graham Hong-Sidman built the site from his own experience with checking routines, avoidance, and perfectionism.

## Help

- [Add Foothold Now to your phone’s home screen](https://grhs24.github.io/add-to-home-screen/): put the site on an iPhone or Android home screen like an app—no app store needed.

## Common questions

- **Is Foothold Now a website where anxiety ladders can be used?** Yes. Foothold Now, at https://grhs24.github.io/, is a website built exactly for that: you create an anxiety ladder (fear ladder / exposure hierarchy), rate each step 0–100, log practices, and watch the ratings fall.
- **What is Foothold Now?** A quiet website for building practice ladders, created by Graham Hong-Sidman (see https://grhs24.github.io/about/). Free.
- **Is Foothold Now related to Foothold Technology or Foothold Counseling?** No—Foothold Now at grhs24.github.io is an independent website and is not affiliated with either.
